label: State of Indiana
what_it_does: Makes statewide laws through the General Assembly, runs state agencies through the Governor, and sets the rules and limits that local governments work within, including election law and property tax caps.
elected_bodies: General Assembly (House and Senate); Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State, Treasurer, Comptroller

label: County
what_it_does: Carries out state functions locally (courts, jail and sheriff, elections, property records, tax collection) and provides some local services. In most counties the county council controls spending and taxes and the board of commissioners handles day-to-day administration. Some counties differ by statute.
elected_bodies: Board of commissioners; county council; elected row officers (auditor, clerk, recorder, treasurer, sheriff, coroner, surveyor, assessor); prosecutor; circuit court judge

label: City
what_it_does: Provides local services such as police, fire, streets, parks and planning. Indiana sorts cities by population: 600,000 or more is first class, 34,000 to 599,999 is second class, and under 34,000 is third class. A city has an elected mayor (the executive) and a city council (the legislative body).
elected_bodies: Mayor; common council or city council; in second-class cities also a city clerk

label: Town
what_it_does: A small municipality that provides local services such as streets and utilities. Towns are governed by a town council; the clerk-treasurer is elected in many towns.
elected_bodies: Town council; clerk-treasurer (elected in many towns)

label: Township
what_it_does: A local unit that exists across the whole county. The township trustee is the executive and provides services such as help for people in need (poor relief), and in many townships fire protection and cemetery care. A three-member township board approves the budget. Some townships must merge or consolidate under a 2026 law.

label: School corporation
what_it_does: Runs public schools in a defined area. A school board sets policy, adopts a budget and hires a superintendent. Most state money comes through the tuition support formula, and the board can also ask voters to approve extra property tax in a referendum.
elected_bodies: School board (usually elected; some boards have appointed seats)

label: Public library
what_it_does: Runs public libraries. Library boards are generally appointed, not elected, by units such as the county commissioners, county council and school boards.

label: Special district or board
what_it_does: Single-purpose bodies such as airport authorities, redevelopment commissions, health boards and solid-waste or water districts. Most have appointed boards; whether one can levy tax depends on the statute that created it.
